context:
Goal: the batch runner keeps handed-in PRs up to date with main, and never clashes with a lane that is still working on the same branch.
Problem (rule): on 13:12 CST Nov 13 you answered "a" to a standing-grant question: the batch runner may add the newest main into a handed-in PR branch (a plain merge, no rebase, no force push). The text drafted from it adds one safety rule: only if no lane has pushed to that branch in the last 2 hours. The coordinator cannot tell whether you saw "2 hours" or it was added later. Your last comment says the options did not make sense; this is the question again, in plain words, with new options.
What is at stake: git itself refuses a push that would overwrite a lane's newer work, so nothing is lost either way. The rule only decides how often the runner and a lane collide, and how long a PR waits.
Based on (read): the grant line in draft PR #3233 (the coordinator read it 22:24 CST), and your "a" in ruling runner-merge-main-grant.
Departs from: main — main has no grant for this at all; the draft adds one.
Meanwhile: nothing changes; the grant waits in the draft.
home: ruling runner-merge-main-grant; draft #3233 (.claude/CLAUDE.md Standing grants; docs/decisions/standing-merge-grant.md)
lastAnswer: 806: d, handed-in only, no clock (23:40 CST Nov 13).

options.gain: No clock and no extra check; it fits how lanes already report to the runner.
options.label: No extra rule: the runner touches only a PR a lane has handed in, and a lane that pushes again says so first (my reading of your note)
options.lose: If a lane forgets to say it is pushing again, a collision is possible (git refuses to overwrite, so nothing is lost).

options.gain: Simple, and a lane that is actively pushing is never disturbed.
options.label: The runner only touches a branch nobody has pushed to for 2 hours
options.lose: A PR can wait up to 2 hours for the newest main. The number is a guess, and a lane that goes quiet for 2 hours but is still working can still collide.

options.gain: No waiting; it only skips a branch that really changed. No made-up number.
options.label: The runner looks at the branch right before it updates it, and skips it if anything new was pushed since it last looked (recommended by the coordinator)
options.lose: The runner makes one extra check per update. A lane that pushes in the seconds right after the check can still collide, though git will refuse to overwrite it.

options.gain: A lane always knows before its branch changes.
options.label: The runner asks the lane (or the coordinator) first and updates only after a yes
options.lose: Slower, and one more message per PR; it is the opposite of the speed you asked of the runner.

reply: Closed on your d. The coordinator is asked to have the grant text in draft #3233 drop the 2 hours.
short: How the runner avoids stepping on a lane's branch
title: When the batch runner brings the newest main into a PR's branch, how does it know a lane is not still working there?
why: The grant you said yes to has a rule to avoid clashing with a lane, and its "2 hours" was never your number.
